correctness.rationale: Every r-subset occupancy word has zeroes and twos in equal numbers. Edges require coordinatewise complementary occupancies, giving precisely the fixed all-ones categorical graph product and, for nonfixed words, the product with a complete bipartite graph K_{e_F,e_Z}. Connected nonbipartite factors permit common sufficiently long walks of either parity, making each component connected; counting product edges gives E=2^{r-1}P for the fixed word, E=2^{r-2k}P otherwise, and rank E-V+1. Involution-orbit count (T_r+1)/2 follows by Burnside. All face-extension and B-empty boundary cases checked logically; no infinite claim follows from finite tests.
